title: Closing questions about future goals and Asian-American jazz labels
summary: Rowe asks about future goals; Jang says he feels satisfied to talk at length and that the Asian-American jazz label is not central for him.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: And also I want to connect it with Max Roach’s honoring of Sid Catlett.

Okay. Well our tape is going to run out soon. I wanted to say, or ask, if we did Part III interview at some point in a few years, is there something that you would like to be able to say that I accomplished this, between now and a few years from now. Do you have some specific goal you’re working on right now?

Well I — what I think is we should — I’m really glad that you’re going to be able to make the “Traditions Transformation” presentation. Because out of this interview, you know I could talk story, music story, for a long time. So I think it’s more like I need to show you more of what I’m doing and then that’s going to come up with some other questions. Now whether I directly address them or maybe I take an improvisation in another direction — and I am improvising. I mean of course it’s all a lot of content information that I accumulated over the years, and they go in like different directions. And they’re always going to go in different directions. So I can’t really answer that. But I will tell you that I feel very satisfied because I generally don’t get a chance to do these kind of interviews where you’d allow me to talk. Because a lot of times I’m already categorized. Or if someone asked me about, you didn’t even use the term “Asian- American jazz” — which I don’t — you know my colleagues and friends Anthony Brown and Mark Izu, that’s very important to them.
